summary: Any deleted non-test file that no test selects is cleared with 'no remaining test references it' and owes no lane, even when surviving non-test code still imports it. A deletion that breaks an untested importer now passes `lanes`, where main failed it with PREGATE_NO_LANE, and the message wrongly says nothing references the file.
evidence: removedPath: `if (!isTestFile(file)) return { removed: { file, note: 'no remaining test references it', lostCoverage: [] }, suite: [] };` never checks for surviving dependents. Scratch repro with the pregate-fixture helper: base has lib/helper.js and lib/consumer.js (which does require('./helper.js')), no tests for either; the branch deletes lib/helper.js. On this branch, lanes prints `pass ... 1 removed path(s)` with `removed (no lane owed): lib/helper.js — no remaining test references it`. On main (temporary worktree) the same repro prints `fail PREGATE_NO_LANE 1 touched file(s) with no test lane: lib/helper.js`.

summary: Any path that is a rename's old name is treated as removed even when a new file exists there again (committed `git mv A B` plus a new untracked A). buildGraph drops it from the tree and test set, and removedPath says it owes no lane ('old name of B'). An untested new source file passes instead of failing PREGATE_NO_LANE, and a new test at that path is never selected or run.
evidence: Scratch fixture run against this branch and a main worktree. (1) mv lib/util.js->lib/util2.js committed, new untracked lib/util.js: main gives FAIL 'lib/util.js has no test lane' (PREGATE_NO_LANE); branch gives 'removed (no lane owed): lib/util.js — old name of lib/util2.js' with no NO_LANE. (2) mv test/util.test.js->test/util-renamed.test.js committed, new untracked failing test/util.test.js: main runs `node --test 'test/util-renamed.test.js' 'test/util.test.js'`; branch runs only `node --test 'test/util-renamed.test.js'`. Cause: `gone` comes from renamedFrom without checking the path is absent; import-graph.ts filters `all` by `gone`; seeds.set(renamedFrom, 'renamed to …') overwrites the 'touched' seed.
